phase.name: Local AI portability and daily-use integration

model_runtime.message: Phase 6 is in progress through IMP-094. Offline Ollama session import, explicit text-only loopback capture, the accepted bounded local-portability migration drill, the deterministic shutdown escape bundle, bounded ChatGPT selected-history import, imported-context replay with accepted primary Intel Mac evidence, bounded local draft/revise/summarize/translate workflows, explicit data-only state context, bounded local work-item proposals, explicit local portability review, structured local runtime failure guidance, a deterministic read-only doll doctor, explicit local full-text state search, explicit local UTF-8 text and Markdown reading, explicit local CSV inspection and transformation, optional local PDF text extraction, optional local image OCR, text/Markdown writing attachment integration, PDF writing attachment integration, OCR image writing attachment integration, CSV writing attachment integration, multiple-attachment writing integration, bounded Lite client resource measurement mechanics, a derived rebuildable RecallState boundary, deterministic weighted lexical memory ranking, an optional rebuildable exact-token memory lexical sidecar, a deterministic fabricated recall-usefulness benchmark, and a bounded local semantic recall candidate harness, an inspectable lexical memory context-budget preview, a review-only memory consolidation candidate detector, and an offline PAM v1.0 staged memory import adapter are implemented. The IMP-063/IMP-064 writing workflow passes at both CI and real-machine evidence levels. IMP-076 uses an invocation-only in-process pypdf adapter; encrypted documents fail closed, pages without extractable text are reported without OCR, and no source overwrite, output file, persistence, model execution, process launch, network access, native-path disclosure, or automatic context injection occurs. IMP-077 uses the optional macOS Vision OCR path with hosted CI execution and no broadened primary real-machine claim. IMP-080 reuses IMP-077 so one explicit PNG or JPEG can replace inline, text/Markdown, or PDF primary source material for revise, summarize, or translate; recognized lines remain data-only untrusted content, use OCR acquisition provenance, preserve adapter order, and must also satisfy the existing 16,000-character writing-source limit before source-origin creation. IMP-083 measures only doll Lite client overhead through a fixed local-only workload with exact tracked-checkout guards, bounded workspace traversal, platform RSS adapters, and privacy-safe synthetic CI evidence; it does not define RAM, disk, or latency requirements and does not measure Ollama or model memory. IMP-084 derives recall output from the accepted non-secret IMP-073 memory search surface, binds results to authoritative MemoryRecord and Doll State revisions, exposes explicit algorithm/version identity and deterministic ranking, and passes MCON-001/MCON-002 without a persistent recall record, usage signal, embedding, model call, network path, or authoritative memory mutation. IMP-085 makes the version-1 weighted-memory-fields policy the default RecallState ranking over the same active, non-secret IMP-073 candidate surface, using inspectable deterministic weighted lexical scoring across subject, content, metadata-only fallback evidence, and exact-phrase bonuses; existing IMP-084 algorithms remain available for rollback, and no persistent recall record, usage signal, index, embedding, model call, network path, automatic context injection, or authoritative memory mutation is introduced. IMP-086 adds only an optional rebuildable exact-token SQLite sidecar under the private workspace temporary/recall-index area; it is non-authoritative, backup-excluded, bound to workspace and state revision, removable, and fails closed when missing, corrupt, unsupported, wrong-workspace, or stale while the IMP-085 scan path remains available. IMP-087 adds a versioned fabricated benchmark that measures the production IMP-085 scan path and optional IMP-086 index without changing retrieval behavior: the version-1 baseline preserves six lexical cases at recall@1, recall@3, and MRR of 1, records two low-overlap paraphrase cases as explicit semantic opportunities currently missed by lexical retrieval, and keeps secret and archived cases excluded. IMP-087 itself does not add embeddings, semantic/vector retrieval, model calls, network access, automatic context injection, authoritative state, or a semantic dependency claim. IMP-088 adds an opt-in bounded local semantic recall candidate harness that reuses the fixed IPv4 loopback Ollama transport and adds only POST /api/embed; it requires explicit local-only confirmation and an explicit already-installed non-cloud model name, keeps vectors and cosine scores transient and non-authoritative, excludes secret and archived memories, preserves the deterministic IMP-085 lexical fallback, and uses synthetic CI evidence without downloading model weights. It does not make semantic recall a product default, persist embeddings, add a vector database, enable automatic context injection, install or pull models, add cloud fallback, or establish accepted real-model semantic dependency evidence. IMP-089 adds a read-only versioned lexical context-budget preview over IMP-085 RecallState. It recommends only confirmed-memory IDs under explicit UTC validity, sensitivity, item, and character budgets, reuses the existing SelectedWritingContextService planner for size and eligibility checks, binds recommendations to MemoryRecord and Doll State revisions, and exposes bounded selection and exclusion evidence. It does not create InstructionOrigin records, materialize context, infer project membership, run a model, persist preview state, or perform automatic or model-selected context injection. IMP-090 adds a deterministic read-only consolidation-candidate detector over active non-secret confirmed memories. It reports exact duplicates, lexical near-duplicates, compatible extensions, and existing explicit contradiction links for review using versioned normalization and lexical overlap rules. Candidate output is advisory and non-persistent, and detection does not merge, archive, supersede, update, or otherwise change authoritative MemoryRecord state automatically. IMP-091 adds an offline PAM v1.0 staged memory import adapter. It validates caller-provided memory-store JSON bytes without network access, verifies required PAM content hashes using PAM normalization, preserves the exact source SHA-256 plus source memory IDs and provenance, and projects each memory into the existing generic staged-import boundary as external_data. PAM lifecycle, access, confidence, instruction type, relations, embedding references, integrity, signatures, owner, and conversation-index data remain non-authoritative source metadata or explicit mapping notes. It does not create confirmed MemoryRecords, local permissions, policies, work completion, instruction authority, model behavior, embeddings, network access, or PAM export. IMP-092 adds candidate-by-candidate reviewed PAM memory publication: a read-only preview binds the exact staged source, Doll State revision, explicit approve/reject decision, mapping notes, and deterministic plan hash; only an explicit user-controlled approval can create a normal confirmed MemoryRecord with source_type=approved_import, rejection writes nothing, unchanged re-approval reuses the existing record, and changed source identity fails closed. PAM lifecycle, confidence, access, relations, instruction, embedding, signature, and integrity metadata remain non-authoritative and are not converted into Doll authority. IMP-092 does not add automatic approval, implicit batch approval, PAM export, model behavior, cloud behavior, or network access. IMP-093 adds bounded offline PAM v1.0 confirmed-memory export for an explicit caller-selected set of active non-secret MemoryRecords under an explicit caller-supplied PAM owner id. It emits deterministic required PAM fields, reuses the IMP-091 content-hash normalization, preserves Doll record identity separately from PAM content hashing, returns explicit mapping/loss evidence, round-trips emitted bytes through the existing offline PAM stager, and leaves Doll State unchanged even from a fresh read-only repository. Secret or archived memories, invalid or duplicate selections, unsupported target versions, and unavailable IDs fail closed. The result is explicitly PAM memory interchange rather than a Doll State Package or complete continuity export, and IMP-093 does not add automatic workspace export, relation/lifecycle/access conversion, embeddings, integrity/signature blocks, model behavior, cloud behavior, or network access. IMP-094 adds version-1 append-oriented ProjectExperienceRecord semantic work history with observation, hypothesis, attempt, outcome, resolution, and lesson event kinds; explicit user/system/import/model assertion and provenance classes; validated project, optional work-item, evidence, source, related-record, and supersession links; and correction through a linked replacement rather than silent semantic rewrite. It participates in State Package export/import, backup/restore, compatibility, and fresh-process inspection through the existing authoritative-record boundary, while Resume Bundle v1 reports deterministic omission instead of silently changing its payload contract. Project experience does not change ProjectRecord scope, complete or reopen WorkItems, create DecisionRecords, approve procedures/checkpoints, grant policy/permission/capability authority, or make imported/model-proposed claims trusted. MCON-009 is covered, including a failed attempt and later resolution, while experience-aware action blocking remains out of scope until ContinuityPreflight. PDF OCR/scanned-PDF fallback, accessibility presentation, primary Intel Mac Lite resource measurement, performance threshold interpretation, the release soak gate, persistent memory-use signals, supported/default semantic retrieval, persistent embeddings, lexical-semantic fusion, automatic/model-selected context injection, accepted real-model semantic embedding dependency evidence, project-aware memory selection, PLUR/PROJECTMEM adapters, ContinuityPreflight, MCP, cross-platform real OCR adapters, tools, the complete Phase 6 gate, Lite v1.0, target-specific application replacement, and stable general anti-lock-in remain incomplete.
